settings.javaTextInfo:
Java

In this section you can configure the Java version that will be used to start your game. If you don't know what you're doing, don't touch anything in this section.

Java Path
Battly uses an integrated version of Java [Official].
settings.javaTextInfo2: This version is available at the displayed path. You can select another Java executable if your Minecraft version requires it.
settings.ramTextInfo:
In this section you can configure the RAM that will be assigned to your game. This is important for your game to work correctly. If you don't know what you're doing, don't touch anything in this section.

Maximum RAM: Indicates the total amount of RAM assigned to your game. It is recommended that you do not exceed 50% of the total RAM present on your PC for it to work correctly. If the PC has more than 8GB of RAM, it is recommended to assign 3GB. If the PC has 4GB or less, do not assign more than 2GB.

Minimum RAM: Indicates the minimum amount of RAM assigned when starting your game. It is recommended not to set more than 3GB for this value. The typical value is 1GB.

supportConsent.detail: Support staff will be able to review logs and modify files and settings to help you. Accept only if you requested help. Permission lasts 10 minutes and ends when you disconnect or close Battly.
serversTutorial.copy0: Create your server first. Then you can come back here to learn how to manage it.
serversTutorial.copy1: You already have a server. You can manage it from this panel.
serversTutorial.copy2: Choose your server address. Your friends will use it to connect when you share the server.
serversTutorial.copy3: Choose the version of Minecraft that you and your friends are going to use.
serversTutorial.copy4: Use Vanilla to play without mods, Fabric or Forge for mods, and Paper or Spigot for plugins.
serversTutorial.copy5: Latency indicates how long the connection takes. A lower value usually gives a faster response.
serversTutorial.copy6: When you click Create Server, you will see the registration and installation step by step.
serversTutorial.copy7: Start or stop your server from here. Wait for it to finish booting before connecting.
serversTutorial.copy8: Here you see what happens on the server. You can check errors and send commands from the console.
serversTutorial.copy9: Activate the connection for your friends and share the address. From here you can also manage who has access.
serversTutorial.copy10: See connected players and manage access lists on your server.
serversTutorial.copy12: Install content compatible with your server version and software.
serversTutorial.copy13: Browse server files. You can edit settings, export files, and archive what you no longer use.
serversTutorial.copy14: Review the RAM, allowed players, and world options before saving changes.
serversTutorial.copy15: Open logs to investigate errors or share them when you need help.
